page: Microsoft Azure E48a_v4 is an EAv4-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1229 GB solid-state drive (SSD). The virtualization layer is managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is positioned in the bottom 10%, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression fall within average ranges. However, multi-threaded operations show notable strength, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU encryption tests scoring in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, along with Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, consistently register in the average tier. Large-model LLM inference speeds represent a performance tradeoff, with prompt processing on a 70B model and text generation on a 7B model scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48a_v4 offers a high-density memory configuration paired with substantial local SSD storage, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without requiring specialized GPU hardware. The resource allocation is well-suited for relational databases, multi-threaded data processing, enterprise applications, and memory-cached web serving. It is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM inference due to the identified single-core and complex model processing limitations.

Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this memory-optimized instance delivers strong multi-threaded performance, as demonstrated by top-25% scores in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU encryption. Conversely, single-core processing is limited, placing in the bottom 10% on stress-ng benchmarks. Memory bandwidth, Redis operations, and static web serving throughput remain average. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core and local SSD storage, the E48a_v4 is suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, and multi-threaded data processing, while being less optimal for single-threaded workloads or heavy LLM inference.
